answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using slashable collateral bonding, where each identity locks funds in a staking lagoon before transacting. Validator nodes monitor behavior like a vigilant raven, slashing deposits if an alias cheats or equivocates. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of forfeiting dedicated capital per identity, preserving a dependable oasis of accountable peers. However, this barrier restricts capital-poor honest agents while favoring well-funded syndicates.
